`RunIdentity` can collide on ext4: birth time is tick-granular, not nanosecond

## Summary

`RunIdentity` is `(dev, ino, born)`. The doc comment on
`a_recreated_run_is_a_different_identity` scopes the guarantee like this:

> On a platform reporting birth time this is guaranteed; where it does not, the
> identity is `dev`+`ino` and a recreated run CAN in principle collide

That invariant does not hold. On ext4 a platform *does* report a birth time and
a recreated run can **still** collide, because ext4's `btime` advances with the
kernel tick, not with the nanosecond field it is reported in. Two runs created
inside the same tick get a byte-identical `born`, and ext4 hands the same-path
recreate the same inode — so all three fields match.

This is `forge#47` reachable again on a host where the warn-once path never
fires, because `born.is_some()` is true.

## Observed

Building rev `cdf3c8c` on x86_64-linux (ext4, distrobox/Docker container):

```
thread 'review::tests::a_recreated_run_is_a_different_identity' panicked at src/review.rs:13267:9:
assertion `left != right` failed: a recreated run must not read as the same run
  left:  RunIdentity { dev: 12583087, ino: 16790867, born: Some(SystemTime { tv_sec: 1788316485, tv_nsec: 150091970 }) }
 right: RunIdentity { dev: 12583087, ino: 16790867, born: Some(SystemTime { tv_sec: 1788316485, tv_nsec: 150091970 }) }
```

`born` is `Some`, and `tv_nsec` is identical to the digit.

It is nondeterministic which of the two identity tests loses the race. Two
consecutive clean builds of the same derivation failed on different tests:

- run 1: `review::tests::a_recreated_run_is_a_different_identity`
- run 2: `review::tests::an_identity_learned_late_is_adopted_rather_than_left_unknown`

1325 passed / 1 failed both times.

## Minimal reproduction — no drovr involved

Inode reuse for a same-path recreate on ext4:

```console
$ T=$(mktemp -d -p /path/on/ext4)
$ for i in 1 2 3 4; do mkdir -p "$T/r"; stat -c "ino=%i" "$T/r"; rm -rf "$T/r"; done
ino=15238693
ino=15238693
ino=15238693
ino=15238693
```

Same inode every time. A control with distinct paths allocates distinct inodes,
confirming it is reuse of the just-freed one and not a stat artifact:

```console
$ mkdir -p "$T/d1" "$T/d2"; stat -c "ino=%i" "$T/d1" "$T/d2"
ino=15238693
ino=15238694
```

The `born` half: driven from a shell, each iteration lands ~4 ms apart and the
btimes differ —

```
btime=2026-09-02 02:41:28.835685461 +0000
btime=2026-09-02 02:41:28.840685382 +0000
btime=2026-09-02 02:41:28.843685334 +0000
```

~4 ms spacing is the tick period (`CONFIG_HZ=250`), not real nanosecond
resolution. The shell's fork/exec is slow enough to cross a tick every time.
The Rust test does `fs::remove_dir_all` then `make_run` in-process, in tens of
microseconds — comfortably inside one tick — so both creates receive the *same*
btime and the identity collides.

So the failure is not "rare inode reuse". It is: **any in-process
delete-and-recreate of the same path on ext4 collides**, and the test only ever
passes on hosts where something happens to be slow enough between the two.

## Why it matters beyond the test

The tests are the messenger. If two runs can share a `RunIdentity`, the cache
cannot tell them apart, and a stale verdict/`feedback.json` can be served for a
recreated run — the `forge#47` behaviour. It bites hardest exactly where runs
are created and destroyed quickly and programmatically: test harnesses, scripted
runs, CI.

Worse than the no-btime case, which at least warns: here `born.is_some()` is
true, so the code believes it has the strong guarantee it does not have.

## Suggested fix

Stop deriving uniqueness from what the filesystem happens to expose. Mint an
identity drovr controls and store it in the run dir — a random nonce (or a
monotonic generation counter) written at run creation, read back as part of
`RunIdentity`. `(dev, ino, born)` can stay as a cheap fast path, but it should
not be the sole proof of difference.

If a filesystem-only identity has to be kept, the btime comparison should be
treated as valid only when the two values differ by more than the clock
granularity; equal btimes must read as "cannot prove different", not as "same".

## Environment

- drovr `cdf3c8c` (`refs/heads/main`, revCount 1056)
- x86_64-linux, ext4 on LVM, inside a distrobox/Docker container
- `CONFIG_HZ=250` (~4 ms tick)
- Built via nixpkgs `buildRustPackage`; tests run in the nix build sandbox
